newsitem.title: USA: Dow gains but tech stocks slump on profit warnings.
newsitem.headline: Dow gains but tech stocks slump on profit warnings.

text.p: Stocks ended mixed on Tuesday, as blue chips posted moderate gains but technology shares skidded after a new set of profit warnings from companies in the sector.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 22.75 points to 7,312.15 after hitting a session low of 7,254 and then jumping by more than 50 points.
In the broader market, advancing issues outpaced declines by 1,473 to 1,022 on volume of almost 527 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Blue chips were aided by a decline in interest rates, which fuelled a strong advance by financial stocks.
The 30-year Treasury bond rose 12/32, or $3.75 on a $1,000 bond, reducing its yield to 6.87 percent from 6.90 percent at Monday's close.
But the story for technology stocks was far different. The Nasdaq Composite index fell 19.88 points to 1,384.91, hit by steep losses among computer networking stocks.
Triggering the sell-off was a warning late Monday from Cabletron Systems Inc. that its first-quarter earnings would fall well short of Wall Street estimates.

Stock in Cabletron slid 15-5/8 to 30-1/8 on the New York Stock Exchange, and the chilling effect of the warning spread across the sector. Cisco Systems Inc. slipped 3-1/16 to 64-3/4 and Cascade Communications Corp. fell 3-3/8 to 34-5/16.
Analysts said the severe reaction showed investor nerves remain frayed after Friday's surprise warning of disappointing second-quarter results by computer chip bellwether Intel Corp.
"Today looks like a continuation of the reaction -- I'd say overreaction -- to Intel's statement," said Peggy Farley, chief executive at Amas Securities.
"People are still afraid to hold techs and generally buy them for a quick gain, which makes them the last group to gain and the first to go down," she said.

Also late Monday, disk drive maker Seagate Technology Inc. said its fiscal fourth-quarter results would fall short of expectations. Seagate fell 3-3/4 to 38-5/8 and competitor Western Digital Corp. fell 3 to 55-1/4, both in Big Board activity.

Despite the heavy selling in tech stocks, the Dow managed to scrape out a modest gain on the day. Some analysts said the performance was an encouraging one because investors remained selective in their selling.

"The market acted in a very discriminating and intelligent way," said Al Goldman, technical analyst at A.G. Edwards and Sons. "Companies that have disappointed are getting punished, but money is still going after other companies."
But analysts also noted Tuesday's action may make investors even more selective about their holdings, particularly in high-growth, high-valuation sectors like technology.

"This certainly raises some caution," said Charlie Crane, chief market strategist at Key Asset Management. "One has to be very certain about earnings prospects, both long- and short-term, because valuations right now are so high."
Among the strongest Dow stocks was J.P. Morgan & Co. Inc., up 2-1/8 to 108-7/8 amid the financial stocks rally. Citicorp climbed 2-3/8 to 115-1/2 and Chase Manhattan Corp. gained 2-1/2 to 97.

Boston Chicken Inc. fell 1 to 15-1/8. Morgan Stanley downgraded the shares a day after the company said it would cut jobs at its headquarters and post a second-quarter severance charge of about $4 million. The company also said it may slow its current growth plans.

RF Micro Devices Inc. jumped 3-5/16 to 15-5/16 on its first day of trading. The company, which makes radio frequency integrated circuits for wireless communications, launched a 3 million-share initial public offering.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 0.88 point to 845.48. The American Stock Exchange index rose 1.85 to 609.02.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 0.82 to 442.36, a record. The average price per share rose 8 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 8,033.576, down 10.879, or 0.14 percent.
